svg.text: Everyday English - Small talk
How are you settling in?
MEANING
A friendly way to ask how someone is adjusting to a
new home, job or community.
IN CONTEXT
You have been in the neighborhood for a couple of
weeks now. How are you settling in?
USAGE NOTE
Settling in focuses on becoming comfortable, rather
than just arriving. Follow up on what the person
chooses to share; avoid pressing for private details.
CONVERSATION
A: How are you settling in?
B: Pretty well, thanks. I am still learning my way
around.
A: Have you found a favorite coffee spot yet?
B: Not yet. Any recommendations?
A: The place near the library is quiet and friendly.
B: That sounds ideal. Is it within walking distance?
A: Yes, about ten minutes from your building.
B: Great. I will try it this weekend. Thanks for the tip.
YOUR TURN
Practice a warm opening and one follow-up
question that fits the answer, without turning the
conversation into an interview.
